name: Workover BOP stack (cut-away)
function: The stack of preventers on the tubing head while the rig has pipe in the hole: adapter, drilling spool with kill and choke outlets, double ram preventer (pipe rams and blind rams), annular preventer, and bell nipple.

tabs.overview: Bottom to top: the adapter flange on the tubing head, a drilling spool whose two side outlets take the kill line and the choke line, a double ram body with pipe rams below (closed on the tubing profile in the cut-away) and blind rams above (open), the annular preventer whose piston squeezes a rubber element inward to seal on any pipe or the open hole, and a bell nipple with the flowline nipple that returns fluid to the tanks. Each ram has a bonnet and a hydraulic operator each side; the annular closes from below its piston. All of it is closed from the accumulator unit at the remote panel or the driller's panel.
tabs.engineering: Preventers per API Spec 16A; stack arrangement, test pressures, and closing times per API Std 53; the 7-1/16 in. 5K class shown suits most land completions.
tabs.connections: Tubing head below (WH); kill line and choke line on the spool (FB choke manifold on workovers); accumulator hydraulic lines; bell nipple flowline to the tanks.
tabs.safety: Pressure tested after nipple up; function tested each shift; the annular is closed first on a kick with pipe across it, rams second.
tabs.evidence: API Spec 16A (S48), API Std 53 (S49), API RP 16ST (S53), field practice (S9). Generic geometry; not an OEM design.
tabs.operations: Nipple up on the tubing head after the tree comes off, test, run or pull pipe, nipple down before the tree goes back on.
tabs.failure_modes: Element wear, ram packer damage, bonnet seal leaks, operator seal leaks, hydraulic hose damage.
